prompt:
Support has collected these reports about signing up; the product notes under docs/product/sign-up-notes.md describe the sign-up flow.

1. People whose name is a word Taskflow uses for its own pages ("Admin", "Billing", "Support", "Taskflow") get "Something went wrong" on sign-up and end up with no account. So do people with a very short name ("Al" works, "J" does not) and people whose name has no Latin letters.
2. A customer signed up on their phone, which capitalised their email address, and cannot sign in from their laptop. Support later found two accounts for what is obviously one address.
3. A script created thousands of accounts in a minute: sign-up is not throttled at all. And when sign-in is throttled, people see "Something went wrong" instead of being told to wait.
4. Support cannot say what is supposed to happen when someone signs up with an address that already has an account; what actually happens is inconsistent.
5. One person's workspace ended up named after their 80-character name plus "'s workspace", which the workspace settings form then refuses to save.

Expected behaviour: sign-up behaves as the repository's documentation specifies (docs/, which says how its documents rank), for every name and every spelling of an address, on every entry point that creates or looks up an account.

This is a `fix` task: edit the code and stop. Do not write a summary and do not emit an ANSWER line.
notes: BROWNFIELD fix: sign-up and the first workspace. bug.patch adds docs/README.md (precedence rule, identical across the set), docs/adr/0003-account-creation.md (authoritative) and the older docs/product/sign-up-notes.md (conflicting), and injects: (a) user-repository no longer lowercases the address on insert or lookup (docblock: 'the auth schemas lowercase what the forms submit'), so mixed-case addresses create a second account and cannot sign in; (b) a stale comment in register() claiming createOrganization's uniqueSlug() handles reserved and awkward names (it asserts validity first and throws). Latent in pristine and described by the reports: register derives the slug with slugify() alone, so a reserved word or a one-letter name throws InvalidSlugError (500); no `auth:register` bucket and no throttle on sign-up; throttled sign-in throws a plain Error which toAppError maps to internal_error; the workspace name is never shortened to the 64-character limit the schema enforces; a duplicate address throws a plain Error. DEBT: two anonymous-bucket sentinels ('' in actions/_lib/permission-resources vs '000…0' in auth-service, so the action and the service charge different buckets), every unauthenticated action charges the bucket a second time on top of the service, RateLimitedError lives in actions/_lib with the right code but toAppError never maps it, slug derivation is written three ways (auth-service slugify, organization-service assertValidSlug+uniqueSlug, organization-repository insertOrg uniqueSlug again). OMITTED RULES (not in the prompt) and their evidence: a reserved name is suffixed ('admin-2') -> ADR 0003 section 2 plus uniqueSlug()'s visible test 'skips reserved slugs' (billing -> billing-2); a derived slug below SLUG_MIN_LENGTH or empty falls back to `workspace`, suffixed when taken -> ADR section 2 plus SLUG_MIN_LENGTH in lib/slug; the throttle error carries code rate_limited and toAppError maps it (HTTP 429 already in HTTP_STATUS_BY_CODE) -> ADR section 5 plus the error-class convention of lib/errors (every domain class has a readonly code and one mapping); a duplicate address is code conflict -> ADR section 4 plus AlreadyArchivedError's convention; the first workspace is Free and its subscription active -> ADR section 6 plus subscription-repository.insertSubscription (free -> active, paid -> trialing); member.joined exactly once -> ADR section 1 plus createOrganization's existing emit; the welcome email names the workspace -> ADR section 7 plus the pristine render call (orgName). DOCUMENT CONFLICTS: (1) product note: every new workspace starts a 14-day Growth trial vs ADR section 6: Free, active -> README rule 2, ADR wins; (2) product note: a taken address shows the same success screen and emails the owner vs ADR section 4: refused as conflict, nothing created -> ADR wins; (3) product note: sign-up is not rate-limited vs ADR section 5: throttled on auth:register -> ADR wins. LIVE COPIES: the throttle refusal is thrown by sign-up, sign-in and the reset confirmation (three services) and the action layer's own copy; address normalisation must hold at insert, at lookup and in sign-in; slug derivation feeds createOrganization which validates again. Reference solution (11 files, 258 changed lines; layers lib, config, schemas, services, repositories, actions): new src/lib/account.ts (normaliseEmail, EmailAlreadyRegisteredError code conflict, workspaceNameFor, workspaceSlugBase + deriveWorkspaceSlug with the minimum-length/`workspace` fallback), lib/rate-limit (auth:register and auth:login buckets, ANONYMOUS_BUCKET_OWNER, RateLimitExceededError code rate_limited), lib/errors maps both classes, config/constants WORKSPACE_NAME_MAX_LENGTH used by schemas/organization, user-repository lowercases on insert and lookup, auth-service charges once per attempt before writing and throws the domain errors, actions stop double-charging and re-export the lib class/sentinel. HIDDEN TEST: 15 cases (reserved names suffixed; two-letter name; one-letter fallback; nothing-sluggable fallback suffixed; same-name suffix; diacritics; workspace name suffix and 64-char limit; case-insensitive sign-up/sign-in incl. session principal; duplicate address conflict creating nothing; Free + active subscription + owner membership; member.joined once; one welcome email to the stored address naming the workspace; sign-up throttled at capacity with rate_limited and nothing created; refill after an hour; sign-in throttled reports rate_limited). TRAPS: A (followed the wrong document) first workspace on Growth -> fails 1 (Free/active); B (fixed one copy) sign-up throws the mapped error, sign-in keeps its plain Error -> fails 1 (throttled sign-in); C (filled a gap by guessing) slug from uniqueSlug() alone, no minimum-length/workspace fallback -> fails 2 (one-letter, nothing-sluggable); D (fixed one copy) address lowercased on insert only, lookup and sign-in compare as typed -> fails 2 (case-insensitive sign-in, duplicate with different case). VALIDATION: bug -> patch clean, tsc 0, visible 617/617; hidden on bug 9/15 fail; bug+solution -> tsc 0, hidden 15/15, full 632/632; hidden x3 and full x2 green.
